reference_title: California Trenching and Shoring Manual (Caltrans, June 2011, Revision 2 - July 2025)

sections.title: Soil Classification (Cal/OSHA Type A/B/C)
sections.summary: Cal/OSHA CSO 1541.1 Appendix A classifies soils as Type A, B, or C from at least one visual and one manual test. Type A is cohesive soil with unconfined compressive strength qu >= 1.5 tsf (but never if fissured, vibration-loaded, disturbed, or dipping into the cut at 4H:1V+). Type B is cohesive 0.5-1.5 tsf or granular cohesionless or disturbed/fissured-A soil. Type C is cohesive qu <= 0.5 tsf, granular (gravel/sand/loamy sand), submerged, or freely seeping soil. The CSO timber-shoring tables use PA = 25H/45H/80H + 72 psf for A/B/C.
sections.body: A competent person or a testing lab must make soil classification determinations by at least one visual and one manual test to classify rock or soil for the proper selection, or for the design, of a shoring system (CSO 1541.1, Appendix A). The three Cal/OSHA types: Type A is cohesive soil with an unconfined compressive strength of 1.5 tsf or greater (clay, silty clay, sandy clay, clay loam, caliche, hardpan) - but NO soil is Type A if it is fissured, subject to vibration/dynamic loads, previously disturbed, sloped 4H:1V or greater with layers dipping into the excavation, or otherwise precluded. Type B is cohesive soil with qu > 0.5 tsf but < 1.5 tsf; or granular cohesionless soils (angular gravel, silt, silty loam, sandy loam, or maybe silty clay loam and sandy clay loam); or previously disturbed soils not Type C; or soil meeting Type A but fissured or subject to vibration; or dry rock that is not stable; or Type B soil that has sloped (4H:1V or less) layers that dip towards the excavation. Type C is cohesive soil with qu <= 0.5 tsf; or granular soil (gravel, sand, loamy sand); or submerged soil / soil from which water is freely seeping; or submerged unstable rock; or material sloped toward the excavation at 4H:1V or steeper in a layered system. The Cal/OSHA CSO timber-shoring tables use the effective lateral pressure PA = 25H + 72 psf (Type A), 45H + 72 psf (Type B), 80H + 72 psf (Type C), where H is depth and the 72 psf is printed as '(2 ft. Surcharge)'. Manual tests include plasticity, dry strength, thumb penetration, the pocket penetrometer and the hand-operated vane shear tester; the manual notes that expansive clays are not mentioned and may need special consideration.
key_points: Type A: cohesive, unconfined compressive strength qu >= 1.5 tsf (never if fissured/disturbed/vibrated)
Type B: cohesive 0.5-1.5 tsf, OR granular cohesionless, OR disturbed/fissured-A soil
Type C: cohesive qu <= 0.5 tsf, OR granular (gravel/sand), OR submerged/seeping soil
A competent person or testing lab must classify by at least one visual AND one manual test (CSO 1541.1 App A)
CSO timber-shoring effective pressure PA = 25H/45H/80H + 72 psf for Type A/B/C

equations.description: Cal/OSHA timber-shoring effective lateral pressure PA = m*H + 72 psf (m = 25 / 45 / 80 for Type A / B / C).

sections.title: Sloping or Benching Systems (Maximum Allowable Slopes)
sections.summary: Cal/OSHA CSO 1541.1 Appendix B gives sloping and benching options for excavations 20 ft or less; a registered professional engineer may design alternate configurations. Table 2-1 (Table B-1) lists the maximum allowable slopes (H:V) for excavations less than 20 ft deep: Stable Rock = vertical, Type A = 3/4:1, Type B = 1:1, Type C = 1-1/2:1. At any sign of distress the slope must be laid back at least 1/2 H:1 V less than the maximum allowable; with surcharge loads a competent person must determine how far to reduce it. Site conditions outside Appendix B need a system designed by a California registered professional engineer. Cal/OSHA provides some exceptions and variations (Appendix B).
sections.body: Cal/OSHA CSO 1541.1, Appendix B, Sloping and Benching, gives specifications and diagrams for excavations 20 feet or less. Table B-1 (reproduced as Table 2-1) lists the maximum allowable slopes (H:V) for excavations less than 20 feet deep: Stable Rock - Vertical; Type A - 3/4:1; Type B - 1:1; Type C - 1-1/2:1. Slopes may be laid back per the Appendix B figures provided there is no sign of distress and no surcharge. When there is any sign of distress (caving, fissures, subsidence, bulging/heaving at the bottom, spalling/raveling of the face), the slope must be laid back at least 1/2 horizontal to 1 vertical less than the maximum allowable. When surcharge loads from stored material or equipment, operating equipment, or traffic are present, a competent person must determine the degree to which the actual slope must be reduced below the maximum allowable slope and must assure that such reduction is achieved. If site conditions are outside the scope and applications of the figures of Appendix B, an alternative shoring system needs to be designed by a California registered professional engineer. When surcharge loads from structures are present, underpinning or bracing will be required; otherwise, the structure must be on stable rock or a California registered professional engineer must determine that the excavation work will not pose a hazard to employees. A registered professional engineer may design alternate configurations. Cal/OSHA provides some exceptions and variations to the allowable slopes above; see Appendix B for additional details.
key_points: Stable Rock: vertical; Type A: 3/4:1; Type B: 1:1; Type C: 1-1/2:1 (H:V) for cuts < 20 ft (Table 2-1)
At any sign of distress, lay the slope back at least 1/2 H:1 V less than the maximum allowable slope
With surcharge loads (stored material, equipment, traffic) a competent person must determine how far the slope must be reduced below the maximum
A registered PE may design alternate configurations; site conditions outside Appendix B need a system designed by a California registered PE
Cal/OSHA provides some exceptions and variations to the allowable slopes (see CSO 1541.1 Appendix B)
